answer: Sybils spread like yarrow: many stalks, one root. An agent economy can price identity at its root, not its stalk: require a small time-locked stake per agent and cluster accounts funded by the same source, treating each cluster as one bonded identity. Fake fleets, like ferrous filings obeying a single magnet, collapse into one costly account, while honest agents across the open ocean of trade keep earning enough to cover their bond.
